The scaled dot-product attention formula in the Transformer is defined as:

$ \text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V $

This calculation involves computing the dot products of the query with all keys, dividing each by $\sqrt{d_k}$, and applying a softmax function to obtain the weights on the values [attention_v7, page 4].

The query-key dot products are divided by $\sqrt{d_k}$ to counteract the effect of dot products growing large in magnitude for larger values of $d_k$. When $d_k$ is large, these large magnitudes "pushing the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients" [attention_v7, page 4]. This ensures that "the predictions for position _i_ can depend only on the known outputs at positions less than _i_" [attention_v7, page 3].

This masking is implemented "inside of scaled dot-product attention by masking out (setting to _−∞_ ) all values in the input of the softmax which correspond to illegal connections" [attention_v7, page 5]. The paper notes that this masking is combined with the fact that "output embeddings are offset by one position" to ensure the dependency constraint [attention_v7, page 3].

Based on the provided passages, each layer in the Transformer encoder and decoder contains a fully connected feed-forward network that is "applied to each position separately and identically" [attention_v7, page 5]. This network consists of two linear transformations with a "ReLU activation in between," as given by the equation "FFN( x ) = max(0 , xW 1 + b 1) W 2 + b 2" [attention_v7, page 5].

Regarding the dimensions, the "dimensionality of input and output is _d_ model = 512", and the "inner-layer has dimensionality _dff_ = 2048" [attention_v7, page 5].

**Why positional encoding is required**
The Transformer requires positional encoding because the model "contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence" [attention_v7, page 6].

As detailed in the training stages section, this involves training on a "single stream of audio" with a batch size covering "16 hours of audio" [moshi_v1, page 20]. To prevent catastrophic forgetting, the model also trains on "text only data from the same dataset as used for Helium" for half of the time [moshi_v1, page 20].
